domain_label: Ludhiana Knitwear Cluster Operating Economics & Political Economy
purpose: A session-bounded method for a compliant export D2C woollen/acrylic knitwear brand to model what it really costs to operate in or source from the Ludhiana cluster, by separating the paper cost stack (yarn/material-dominated, anchored on Vardhman's FY20 54%-of-revenue raw-material disclosure) from the compliance premium a paper-clean entrant carries (EPF+ESI loading, GST inverted-duty working-capital trap, effluent/CETP closure risk, the regulatory headcount thresholds) and from the off-paper layer, described strictly as a structural mechanism with every rupee amount held at UNKNOWN, then costing the migrant piece-rate labour reality and the winter-seasonal working-capital and labour-retention twin shocks, so the owner budgets the compliance premium as a named line item rather than competing on a cost edge it can never win.
assumptions: no unit-level Ludhiana purchasing or payroll dataset is supplied; cost-share weights are anchored estimates keyed to the Ludhiana deep-dive (sec 4-5), not invoices
the operator is a small compliant export D2C woollen/acrylic (MMF-leaning) knitwear brand selling in California/Turlock, NOT a price-driven commodity exporter
the only hard public-disclosure FACT anchor is Vardhman Textiles FY20 raw material consumed = 54% of revenue; every other cost-share is a labeled estimate
the single most-wanted bottom-up labour input, the per-piece sweater piece-rate, is UNKNOWN and is never fabricated
off-paper magnitudes are UNKNOWN by design; the layer is treated as how clusters of this type are generally reported to operate, never as an accusation against any named person or firm
the large listed/audited cluster firms (Vardhman, Monte Carlo, Nahar) operate under public-disclosure regimes and no claim is made about their conduct
exclusions: any assertion that a named person or firm pays bribes, evades tax, or is politically captured (off-paper is mechanism-only, all amounts UNKNOWN)
any fabricated revenue, earnings, or piece-rate figure for a named firm stated as fact (only publicly-disclosed FACTs or labeled benchmark estimates are used)
yarn count/blend/spec engineering and machine selection (covered by the yarn and machines KBs)
landed-cost, freight, duty, RoDTEP/RoSCTL, and unit economics modeling (covered by the logistics/unit-economics KB)
where-to-source location comparison vs Tirupur/Bangladesh/Vietnam/China (covered by the cluster deep-dive and macro KB)
brand, CAC, and D2C demand economics (covered by the brand KB)

competency_questions.question: What does the paper cost stack look like for a Ludhiana knit-garment unit and for a spinning unit, and which single line dominates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MATERIAL_DOMINANCE states yarn/material at ~50-60% as the dominant line anchored on the Vardhman FY20 54%-of-revenue FACT, and KNIT_GARMENT_COST_STACK and SPINNING_COST_STACK give the labelled-estimate breakdowns (knit: yarn ~50-65%, labour ~15-25%, power ~5-10%; spinning: material ~50-60%, power ~12-18%, labour ~8-12%)

competency_questions.question: What is the legal compliance premium a paper-clean entrant carries that an off-roll competitor sheds, and how large is the EPF/ESI piece?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANCE_PREMIUM_FRAME assembles the premium and EPF_ESI_LOADING quantifies the ~15%+ EPF (12%) + ESI (3.25%) loading as the largest single legal cost disadvantage, with the competitor-gap magnitude tagged UNKNOWN

competency_questions.question: How does the GST inverted-duty structure trap working capital, and why does it bite an acrylic/MMF brand specifically?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GST_INVERTED_DUTY states the 12% stitched-garment FACT, the documented inputs-taxed-higher-than-output inversion that traps capital in slow refunds, and that MMF/acrylic yarn is the acute case

competency_questions.question: Why is dyeing the highest-regulatory-risk node, and what is the judgment for a small entrant?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EFFLUENT_CETP_RISK cites the three-non-compliant-CETPs, CPCB crore penalties, NGT review, and deep-well discharge FACTs, and DYEHOUSE_AVOIDANCE states the do-NOT-own-a-dyehouse judgment with the outsource/buy-dyed-yarn alternative

competency_questions.question: Which regulatory headcount thresholds trigger which obligations, and which one never switches off?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATORY_THRESHOLDS lists Factories Act 10+ with power / 20+ without, ESI at 10+, GST above ~Rs40 lakh, and EPF mandatory at 20+ with the once-covered-always-covered lock-in

competency_questions.question: How is the off-paper layer described honestly as a mechanism, and what is the citable literature backbone versus the cluster-specific inference?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OFF_PAPER_LITERATURE_BACKBONE gives the FACT findings of the bribery/inspector-raj literature, OFF_PAPER_CLUSTER_APPLICATIONS lists the six recurring mechanisms as ESTIMATE discussion/industry-lore with all amounts UNKNOWN and no named-party accusation, and HONESTY_TAGGING governs the labeling

competency_questions.question: Why is the off-paper route a low-ceiling risk position rather than free money for a growing export brand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOW_CEILING_RISK states that off-paper carries NGT/CPCB closure exposure, the EPF lock-in, reassessment risk, and rent that scales up with size and visibility, and that the literature finds informality is precisely why these firms cannot grow

competency_questions.question: What is the migrant labour structure, and why is the per-piece sweater piece-rate the number that blocks any honest bottom-up labour cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MIGRANT_LABOUR_STRUCTURE states the ~90-95% migrant workforce and the ~Rs11-13k/month statutory floor, and PIECE_RATE_UNKNOWN marks the per-piece rate as UNKNOWN and the single highest-value missing number, never to be fabricated

competency_questions.question: How does the thekedar contractor layer shape labour cost and enable the off-paper economy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THEKEDAR_LAYER explains contractor-supplied piece-rate migrant crews as the mechanism that keeps wages low and headcount flexible and the layer that absorbs headcount, identity, and cash under the thresholds

competency_questions.question: Which skills are the bottleneck, and why does the CAD/flat-knit-programmer scarcity matter for an AI-design pipeline?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LINKER_PROGRAMMER_BOTTLENECK names linking as the quality-critical, eyesight-intensive, hardest-to-rehire seam and the CAD/Shima-Stoll-class programmer scarcity as the direct flag for translating an AI design into a machine program

competency_questions.question: How does the winter-seasonal calendar produce twin entrant shocks, and what are they?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONAL_CALENDAR states the winter product, July-October ramp, October order-lifting peak and lean trough, and WORKING_CAPITAL_SHOCK and LABOUR_RETENTION_SHOCK characterize the cash-cycle and migrant-return shocks

competency_questions.question: How is every money/capacity/regulation/behaviour claim tagged so no fabricated or accusatory claim survives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONESTY_TAGGING requires each claim tagged FACT (public source), ESTIMATE (method+basis+confidence, literal word estimate), or UNKNOWN, forbids stating as fact that a named party pays bribes/evades/is captured, and forbids fabricated named-firm figures

competency_questions.question: What is the recommended operating posture given that the entrant's edge can never be cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANT_CORE_POSTURE states compliant-core, outsource-the-dirty-node (no dyehouse), and explicitly budget BOTH the compliance-cost premium AND a friction/speed-money line item as named planned costs, with edge on product/brand/export-legitimacy not cost

competency_questions.question: On what triggers is the operating-economics model re-run, and which inputs would most change it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANT_CORE_POSTURE and PIECE_RATE_UNKNOWN feed the review, and the iteration protocol re-runs the cost and premium model when a piece-rate ground figure, a statutory rate, a CETP/NGT enforcement event, or the season changes

glossary.definition: The on-the-books cost structure of a Ludhiana unit: for a knit-garment unit ~50-65% yarn, ~15-25% labour, ~5-10% power, rest dyeing/finishing/overhead/packing; for a spinning unit ~50-60% raw material, ~12-18% power, ~8-12% labour. Only the material-dominance line is anchored on a hard FACT (Vardhman FY20 54% of revenue); the rest are labeled estimates, not measured cluster averages.

The bundle of legal costs a fully paper-clean entrant carries that an off-roll competitor sheds: ~15%+ EPF (12%) + ESI (3.25%) loading on cash wages, full GST with capital trapped in the inverted-duty refund lag, genuine effluent cost if dyeing in-house, and full statutory wages. Direction is HIGH-confidence; the magnitude of the gap versus the price-setters is UNKNOWN.

The gap between paper cost and real cost, described strictly as how clusters of this type are generally reported to operate (speed money, inspector raj, thekedar cash, under-invoicing, political bias, pollution-norm arbitrage). It is a structural mechanism with a citable literature backbone, NEVER an accusation against any named person or firm, and every rupee magnitude in it is UNKNOWN by design.

A labour contractor who supplies and manages migrant piece-rate crews so the owner often does not employ workers directly; the layer that keeps wages low and headcount flexible and that absorbs headcount, identity, and cash, making it the mechanism through which much of the off-paper economy is reported to operate.

A GST configuration where inputs (yarn, especially MMF/acrylic) are taxed relatively higher than the 12% on the stitched-garment output, so the unit accumulates input tax credit it can only recover through slow refunds, trapping working capital. It bites an acrylic/MMF brand specifically.

The EPF rule that once a unit crosses 20 employees and becomes EPF-covered, the obligation never switches off even if headcount later falls below 20; a one-way regulatory lock-in that makes crossing the threshold a permanent commitment.

The quality-critical seam that joins knit panels loop-to-loop at shoulder and side; eyesight-intensive, piece-rate, and where a small unit's quality reputation is won or lost. Skilled linkers are the hardest core role to re-hire after the lean season, making linking the recognized labour bottleneck.

Common Effluent Treatment Plant serving the cluster's dyeing units. All three Ludhiana CETPs were found non-compliant; CPCB levied penalties in crores, the NGT is reviewing petitions, and some units were documented boring deep wells to dump effluent, making dyeing the highest-regulatory-risk node and the basis for the do-NOT-own-a-dyehouse judgment.

The two cash-and-labour stresses the winter-seasonal calendar imposes: a working-capital shock (yarn bought and goods made months before cash returns, receivables stretched across the season) and a labour-retention shock (migrants go home in the lean trough and skilled linkers are the hardest to re-hire), both keyed to the July-October ramp and October order-lifting peak.

The binding label every money/capacity/regulation/behaviour claim carries: FACT (cited public source), ESTIMATE (method + basis + confidence, using the literal word estimate; off-paper variant ESTIMATE: discussion/industry-lore framed as mechanism never accusation), or UNKNOWN (a valid, frequent value). No named-firm figure is fabricated and no named party is alleged to bribe, evade, or be captured.

source_registry.description: anchored-estimate cost and political-economy work units for the Ludhiana woollen/acrylic knitwear cluster, grounded in the Ludhiana deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md sec 4-5): its one hard cost FACT (Vardhman FY20 raw material = 54% of revenue), its anchored knit-garment and spinning cost stacks, its statutory compliance facts (EPF 12% + ESI 3.25% loading, GST 12% on stitched garments with documented inverted-duty structure, Factories Act 10+/20+ and EPF-20+/ESI-10+ thresholds), its cited effluent enforcement record (three Ludhiana CETPs non-compliant, CPCB penalties in crores, NGT review, deep-well discharge), its off-paper literature backbone (MSE WP 291; Sharma & Biswas 2020; ScienceDirect bribery-and-firm-performance; Business Standard Inspector Raj), and its labour/seasonality reality (90-95% migrant workforce, ~Rs438/day ~Rs11,390/month Punjab statutory floor, UNKNOWN per-piece rate, thekedar contracting, linker and CAD/flat-knit-programmer bottlenecks, July-October winter ramp); no supplied unit-level dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Ludhiana Knitwear Cluster Owner Deep-Dive (FACTORY/sweater_vertical/analysis/ludhiana/DEEPDIVE.md sec 4-5; reconciled.md); Vardhman Textiles FY20 annual disclosure (raw material consumed = 54% of revenue); EPFO contribution rate (12% employer) and ESIC rate (3.25% employer); GST 12% on stitched garments and the documented apparel/MMF inverted duty structure (CBIC/AEPC); Factories Act 1948 sec 2(m) 10/20-worker thresholds, EPF Act 20+ once-covered-always-covered, ESI Act 10+; CPCB/NGT Ludhiana CETP non-compliance and Buddha Nullah deep-well-discharge enforcement record; ILO comparative garment wage (~US$145-172/month); Punjab Labour Dept minimum-wage notification (Mar-2025, ~Rs438/day unskilled); off-paper literature backbone (MSE Working Paper 291; Sharma & Biswas 2020; ScienceDirect 'Bribery and firm performance in India'; Business Standard 'Inspector Raj'); anchored estimates where no unit-level dataset exists

nodes.definition: Establish the binding tagging discipline that every downstream money, capacity, regulation, and behaviour claim must carry: FACT for a cited public source, ESTIMATE for a reasoned figure that states method plus basis plus confidence and uses the literal word estimate (with the off-paper variant ESTIMATE: discussion/industry-lore framed as structural mechanism, never accusation), and UNKNOWN where the cluster genuinely does not know, treated as a valid and frequent value. It forbids stating as fact that any named person or firm pays bribes, evades tax, or is politically captured, and forbids any fabricated revenue, earnings, or piece-rate figure for a named firm; only publicly-disclosed FACTs (e.g., Vardhman FY20 54%) or labeled benchmark estimates are permitted. This node is the raw input that governs how every other node may phrase a claim.

excluded: the substantive cost or labour figures themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a public-source FACT supersedes an estimate or a tagging violation is found

pros.claim: A binding tag on every claim keeps the analysis usable for export compliance and prevents an estimate being later quoted as a measured fact or an accusation
pros.example: the Vardhman 54% line stays a FACT while a knit-stack labour share stays a labeled estimate and the off-paper rupee magnitude stays UNKNOWN

cons.claim: Strict tagging makes the prose heavier and leaves many high-interest numbers explicitly UNKNOWN rather than filled
cons.example: the per-piece rate must be left UNKNOWN rather than given a plausible-sounding placeholder

failure_modes: dropping a tag downstream so an estimate hardens into an apparent fact
naming a specific firm as paying bribes or evading tax instead of describing a structural mechanism
acceptance_tests: every money/capacity/regulation/behaviour claim in the KB carries FACT, ESTIMATE (with method+basis+confidence), or UNKNOWN, and no named person or firm is alleged to bribe, evade, or be captured
revisit_triggers: a new public-source FACT supersedes a prior estimate
a downstream node is found stating an estimate or accusation as fact

nodes.definition: Pin the single most structurally load-bearing fact of the cluster's economics: yarn/material is the dominant cost line at ~50-60% in both the spinning stack and the knit-garment stack, anchored on the one hard FACT in the whole analysis, Vardhman Textiles FY20 raw material consumed = 54% of revenue. Everything downstream follows: for a downstream brand, yarn cost and labour dominate while brand margin is captured in distribution, not at the factory gate. The ~50-60% band itself rests on this one anchor plus norms, so it is a labeled estimate (medium) rather than a measured cluster average, while the 54% point is FACT.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a firm-level raw-material disclosure or unit-level cost study updates the anchor

pros.claim: Anchoring material dominance on a single hard FACT tells the brand exactly where the cost is and that it cannot be undercut by squeezing overhead
pros.example: a downstream brand recognizing that shaving labour or packing cannot move a stack that is half yarn, so margin must come from distribution

cons.claim: Leaning the whole stack on one firm's one-year disclosure risks over-generalizing a spinner's ratio to a knit-garment unit
cons.example: treating Vardhman's integrated-spinner 54% as if it were a small knit shop's exact material share

failure_modes: presenting the ~50-60% band as a measured cluster average rather than a one-anchor estimate
ignoring that material dominance means the entrant's edge cannot be input cost
acceptance_tests: material/yarn is stated as the ~50-60% dominant line anchored on the Vardhman FY20 54%-of-revenue FACT, with the band labeled an estimate
revisit_triggers: a newer firm-level raw-material disclosure updates the anchor
a unit-level cost study replaces the estimated band

nodes.definition: Lay out the knit-garment paper cost stack as a labeled estimate (medium): yarn ~50-65%; labour (knitting, linking, finishing, checking) ~15-25%, higher than woven because knitwear is more labour-intensive and linking/finishing is hand-skilled; power ~5-10%; the remainder dyeing/finishing/overhead/packing. This is the stack our downstream brand actually buys into, and it is where the ~15-25% labour share makes the EPF/ESI loading and the piece-rate UNKNOWN materially important. None of these shares is a measured cluster average; they are anchored on the material-dominance FACT plus knitwear norms.

included: why knitwear labour share runs high
excluded: absolute rupee costs and yarn prices

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a knit-garment cost study or product-mix shift updates the stack

pros.claim: A labeled knit-garment stack shows the brand that labour is a real 15-25% line, so the compliance loading on it is not a rounding error
pros.example: an entrant seeing that a 15%+ EPF/ESI loading on a 15-25% labour line is a few points of total cost it cannot shed

cons.claim: The wide bands can be over-read as precise when they are norm-anchored estimates that vary by product and unit
cons.example: treating a cable-heavy fully-fashioned sweater's labour share as identical to a plain jersey's

failure_modes: quoting the bands as measured averages
forgetting that the high labour share is what makes linking and piece-rate the cost-sensitive nodes
acceptance_tests: the knit-garment stack is given as yarn ~50-65%, labour ~15-25%, power ~5-10%, rest finishing/overhead, each labeled an estimate
revisit_triggers: a unit-level knit-garment cost study lands
the product mix shifts the labour or yarn share materially

nodes.definition: Lay out the spinning paper cost stack as a labeled estimate (medium): raw material ~50-60%; power ~12-18%, the #2 line and the reason captive power is decisive for the integrated survivors; labour ~8-12%, lower than knit-garment because spinning is capital- and power-intensive rather than hand-skilled. This stack explains why the big spinners run captive generation and why a yarn-buying entrant, exposed to the grid and buying yarn at market, inherits the spinner's material-and-power exposure without the captive offset. The shares are norm-anchored estimates, not measured averages, sitting on the same material-dominance FACT.

included: why power is the decisive #2 line
excluded: PSPCL tariff specifics which are UNKNOWN

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the PSPCL tariff or a spinning cost study updates the stack

pros.claim: Showing power as the spinning #2 line explains the captive-generation moat and why a grid-exposed entrant cannot match integrated yarn cost
pros.example: an entrant understanding that buying yarn at market embeds the spinner's ~12-18% power line it cannot self-generate around

cons.claim: The power band is sensitive to an UNKNOWN current PSPCL tariff, so the stack is directional not precise
cons.example: a tariff slab change moving the real power share outside the stated band

failure_modes: quoting the bands as measured averages
ignoring that the entrant inherits this stack embedded in market yarn price
acceptance_tests: the spinning stack is given as material ~50-60%, power ~12-18%, labour ~8-12%, each labeled an estimate, with power flagged as the decisive #2 line
revisit_triggers: the current PSPCL industrial tariff becomes known
a spinning cost study updates the shares

nodes.definition: Assemble the legal compliance premium as the real story of the cluster's cost asymmetry, not the bribes: a fully paper-clean entrant carries costs an off-roll competitor sheds, namely the ~15%+ EPF/ESI loading, full GST with capital trapped in the inverted-duty refund lag, genuine effluent cost if it dyes, and full statutory wages, all on top of the regulatory thresholds that trigger them. The compliant unit's landed cost is structurally higher than the cluster's price-setters; the direction is HIGH-confidence and the magnitude of the gap is UNKNOWN. This frame is the umbrella that the EPF/ESI, GST, effluent, and threshold nodes specialize, and it is the line item the owner must budget rather than wish away.

included: the assembled legal premium as a named budget line
excluded: the specific statutory rates handled in child nodes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a statutory rate, threshold, or competitor-gap sizing changes the premium

pros.claim: Framing the premium as legal and budgetable lets the owner plan it as a known line item instead of being surprised or tempted to shed it
pros.example: an export brand pricing in the EPF/ESI + inverted-duty drag from day one rather than discovering it after launch

cons.claim: Because the competitor-gap magnitude is UNKNOWN, the frame states a direction it cannot yet size in rupees
cons.example: knowing the compliant unit is dearer without being able to say by how much versus a specific off-roll competitor

failure_modes: conflating the legal premium with the off-paper layer
treating the gap as zero because its magnitude is UNKNOWN
acceptance_tests: the premium is assembled as the EPF/ESI + GST inverted-duty + effluent + statutory-wage bundle with direction HIGH and gap magnitude UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: a statutory rate or threshold changes
a unit-level cost comparison sizes the competitor gap

nodes.definition: Quantify the largest single legal cost disadvantage versus a contractor-off-roll competitor: EPF at 12% plus ESI at 3.25% gives a ~15%+ statutory loading on cash wages for on-roll labour. The ~15% figure is arithmetic from the statutory rates (HIGH confidence); the magnitude of the gap versus a competitor who runs labour off-roll through a thekedar is UNKNOWN. Because the knit-garment labour share is a real 15-25% of cost, this loading is not negligible, and it is precisely the cost an off-roll competitor sheds, making it the clearest legal piece of the compliance premium.

included: why it is the largest single legal disadvantage
excluded: the GST and effluent premium components
the off-roll competitor's actual behaviour as an accusation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an EPF or ESI contribution rate changes

pros.claim: Pinning the loading to statutory rates gives a HIGH-confidence, budgetable number rather than a guess
pros.example: an entrant adding ~15%+ on every on-roll cash wage to its labour cost as a known line

cons.claim: The loading is precise but the gap it creates versus an off-roll competitor is UNKNOWN, so it sizes the entrant's cost not the competitor's saving
cons.example: knowing the compliant loading is ~15%+ without knowing how much a thekedar-routed competitor avoids

failure_modes: stating the competitor's off-roll saving as a fact rather than UNKNOWN
applying the loading to total cost rather than to the labour line
acceptance_tests: the EPF 12% + ESI 3.25% ~15%+ loading is stated as arithmetic-from-statutory-rates HIGH with the competitor-gap magnitude UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: EPFO or ESIC contribution rates change
a unit-level study sizes the off-roll gap

nodes.definition: Characterize the GST working-capital trap: stitched garments carry 12% GST (FACT), and the sector suffers a documented inverted duty structure where inputs, especially MMF/acrylic yarn, are taxed relatively higher than the output, so the unit accumulates input tax credit recoverable only through slow refunds, trapping working capital. This bites our specific case because an export D2C brand would likely use acrylic/MMF yarn, putting it squarely in the acute inversion. It is a legal, real cost that compounds the seasonal working-capital shock and that a clean entrant cannot avoid by anything other than product/blend choice.

included: why MMF/acrylic is the acute case
excluded: the export RoDTEP/RoSCTL refund mechanics handled in the logistics KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a GST rate or inverted-duty correction changes

pros.claim: Naming the inverted-duty trap warns the brand that its likely acrylic/MMF choice carries a working-capital drag, not just a tax line
pros.example: an acrylic-leaning brand budgeting for refund lag rather than assuming GST is a wash

cons.claim: The magnitude of the trapped capital depends on refund-cycle timing that is not unit-known here
cons.example: knowing capital is trapped without a confirmed days-of-refund-lag figure

failure_modes: treating GST as a neutral pass-through and missing the refund-lag drag
ignoring that the MMF/acrylic blend choice is what triggers the acute case
acceptance_tests: the 12% stitched-garment GST FACT and the inverted-duty working-capital trap are stated with MMF/acrylic flagged as the acute case
revisit_triggers: a GST rate or the inverted-duty correction changes
the brand's fibre/blend choice moves away from MMF

nodes.definition: Establish dyeing as the highest-regulatory-risk node in the entire cluster, on cited FACTs: all three Ludhiana CETPs were found non-compliant, CPCB levied penalties worth crores, the NGT is reviewing fourteen petitions, and some units were documented boring deep wells to dump effluent into Buddha Nullah and the soil. This makes in-house dyeing a closure-and-penalty exposure rather than just a cost, and it is the cluster-level enforcement record behind the do-NOT-own-a-dyehouse judgment. The per-unit CETP/effluent compliance cost is UNKNOWN; only the cluster-level enforcement is FACT.

included: three-non-compliant-CETPs, CPCB crore penalties, NGT review, deep-well discharge FACTs
dyeing as the top regulatory-risk node
excluded: colour-control and supply consequences of outsourcing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an NGT/CPCB action or a per-unit effluent cost figure changes the picture

pros.claim: Documenting the enforcement record converts dyeing from a cost question into a closure-risk question the owner can act on
pros.example: an entrant treating in-house dyeing as a regulatory liability after seeing the CETP non-compliance and NGT record

cons.claim: Cluster-level enforcement FACTs do not give a per-unit compliance cost, which stays UNKNOWN
cons.example: knowing the cluster faces crore penalties without a per-unit effluent-cost figure to budget

failure_modes: reading cluster-level penalties as a per-unit cost
underestimating the closure exposure of in-house dyeing
acceptance_tests: the three-non-compliant-CETPs, CPCB crore penalties, NGT review, and deep-well discharge are cited as FACTs establishing dyeing as the top regulatory-risk node
revisit_triggers: an NGT ruling or CPCB action changes the enforcement posture
a per-unit effluent compliance cost becomes known

nodes.definition: State the binding judgment (HIGH confidence) that a small new entrant should NOT own a dyehouse: outsource dyeing or buy dyed yarn, pushing the CETP-non-compliance, NGT, and crore-penalty closure risk onto suppliers, at the accepted cost of some colour control and supply risk. Going paper-clean on this node is also what unlocks RoDTEP/RoSCTL refunds, clean US import, and any future brand/ESG story, so the judgment is both a risk-avoidance and a legitimacy move. This is the actionable conclusion of the effluent-risk node and a core piece of the compliant-core posture.

included: the colour-control and supply-risk tradeoff accepted
excluded: yarn-shade QC mechanics handled in the quality KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the effluent enforcement posture or a compliant small-scale dyeing option changes

pros.claim: Outsourcing the dirty node pushes closure and NGT risk onto suppliers and keeps the brand paper-clean for export legitimacy
pros.example: an entrant buying dyed yarn so a CETP closure hits its supplier, not its own production line

cons.claim: Outsourcing dyeing surrenders colour control and adds supplier dependence and lot-to-lot shade risk
cons.example: a shade mismatch between dyed-yarn lots the brand can no longer correct in-house

failure_modes: building an in-house dyehouse to chase colour control and inheriting closure risk
outsourcing without a shade-consistency control on incoming dyed yarn
acceptance_tests: the do-NOT-own-a-dyehouse judgment is stated with the outsource/buy-dyed-yarn alternative and the accepted colour-control/supply-risk tradeoff
revisit_triggers: the effluent enforcement posture eases materially
a compliant zero-liquid-discharge dyeing option becomes affordable at small scale

nodes.definition: Establish the headcount and turnover thresholds that trigger compliance obligations (all FACT): the Factories Act applies at 10+ workers with power or 20+ without; ESI applies at 10+ and covers contract workers on premises; EPF is mandatory at 20+ and, once crossed, is once-covered-always-covered so it never switches off; GST applies above ~Rs40 lakh turnover; and Punjab Shops & Establishments registration applies. These thresholds are why the thekedar layer is used to keep on-paper turnover and headcount under the triggers, and the EPF lock-in is the one to watch because crossing it is a permanent one-way commitment.

included: Factories Act 10+/20+, ESI 10+, EPF 20+ once-covered, GST ~Rs40 lakh, Punjab S&E
why thresholds drive the thekedar layer
excluded: the contribution-rate arithmetic handled in EPF_ESI_LOADING
the off-paper threshold-evasion mechanism handled in the off-paper nodes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a statutory headcount or turnover threshold is amended

pros.claim: Listing the exact triggers lets an entrant plan headcount and registration deliberately rather than tripping a lock-in by accident
pros.example: an entrant scaling on-roll headcount knowing 20+ crosses the permanent EPF threshold

cons.claim: The thresholds invite gaming via fragmentation that is itself the low-ceiling trap, so the list can read as an evasion menu if not paired with the risk framing
cons.example: an operator splitting headcount to dodge a threshold and capping its own scale

failure_modes: crossing the EPF 20+ threshold without realizing it is permanent
treating ESI as not applying to on-premises contract workers
acceptance_tests: the Factories Act 10+/20+, ESI 10+, EPF 20+ once-covered-always-covered, and GST ~Rs40 lakh thresholds are listed as FACTs with the EPF lock-in flagged
revisit_triggers: a statutory threshold is amended
the operator's headcount or turnover approaches a trigger

nodes.definition: Establish the citable backbone for the off-paper layer as the FACT findings of the literature, kept strictly separate from any cluster-specific application: India's dense multi-agency regulatory stack is documented to breed inspector rent-seeking, with firms facing bribes in addition to or in lieu of compliance costs, and firms that evaded taxes found to pay higher bribes (MSE Working Paper 291; Sharma & Biswas 2020; ScienceDirect 'Bribery and firm performance in India'; Business Standard 'Inspector Raj'). These are findings-of-the-literature FACTs about Indian firms generally; the Ludhiana-specific applications are separate ESTIMATE inferences and no named cluster firm is implicated.

included: the bribery/inspector-raj literature findings as FACTs
excluded: any rupee magnitude, which is UNKNOWN

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new source updates the literature backbone

pros.claim: Anchoring the off-paper discussion on a published literature backbone keeps it citable and defensible rather than rumor
pros.example: grounding the inspector-raj point on MSE WP 291 and the bribery-performance literature rather than on hearsay

cons.claim: The literature is about Indian firms generally, so it supports a mechanism but cannot prove the cluster-specific or magnitude claims
cons.example: the literature confirming inspector rent-seeking exists nationally without quantifying it in Ludhiana

failure_modes: promoting a literature finding into a cluster-specific or named-firm assertion
attaching a rupee magnitude to the backbone
acceptance_tests: the bribery/inspector-raj literature findings are stated as FACTs with citations, kept distinct from cluster-specific inference and with no rupee magnitude
revisit_triggers: a new peer-reviewed source updates the backbone
a cited source is found to be misread

nodes.definition: Describe the six recurring off-paper mechanisms as ESTIMATE: discussion/industry-lore inferences from the literature backbone, existence MED-HIGH and all amounts UNKNOWN, framed as how clusters of this type are generally reported to operate and never as an accusation against any named person or firm: (1) speed money at discretionary gates (factory licence, pollution consent, electricity load, GST-refund release); (2) inspector raj at periodic labour/boiler/fire/pollution/weights inspections; (3) cash dealing via the thekedar to keep on-paper turnover under threshold; (4) under-invoicing to shrink the tax/duty base; (5) political bias/capture, where AEPC-style lobbying is FACT and legal but selective enforcement relief is the ESTIMATE inference; (6) pollution-norm arbitrage where CETP compliance is costly and enforcement episodic. Each is a structural incentive, not a documented act.

included: the six recurring mechanisms as ESTIMATE discussion/industry-lore

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a mechanism's plausibility or a credible sizing changes

pros.claim: Naming the mechanisms structurally lets the owner anticipate where friction arises without accusing anyone or inventing numbers
pros.example: budgeting for speed-money friction at the pollution-consent and GST-refund gates as a discretionary-delay risk

cons.claim: Because every magnitude is UNKNOWN, the mechanisms inform posture but cannot be costed in rupees
cons.example: knowing under-invoicing is a structural incentive without any prevalence or amount figure to model

failure_modes: stating a mechanism as a named firm's documented act
attaching a fabricated rupee amount to any mechanism
acceptance_tests: the six mechanisms are listed as ESTIMATE discussion/industry-lore with existence MED-HIGH, all amounts UNKNOWN, and no named-party accusation
revisit_triggers: the regulatory or enforcement environment changes a mechanism's plausibility
a credible study sizes a mechanism

nodes.definition: State the crucial owner finding that the off-paper route is a RISK POSITION, not free money: it carries NGT/CPCB closure exposure, the EPF once-covered-always-covered lock-in, GST/income reassessment risk, and rent that scales up with size and visibility (larger firms pay more). The literature's core finding is the kicker: informality is precisely why these firms cannot grow, because it disincentivizes fixed investment and caps scale. So the arbitrage is not a growth strategy but a low-ceiling survival strategy, and an export D2C brand, which needs clean docs for RoDTEP/RoSCTL and US import and is the one segment where the bribery-performance literature finds less negative impact, should not build its model on it.

included: off-paper as a risk position not free money

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an enforcement or export-incentive shift changes the informality risk-reward

pros.claim: Reframing off-paper as a low-ceiling risk dissolves the temptation to treat it as a cost edge and aligns with export legitimacy
pros.example: an export brand declining off-paper arbitrage because clean docs unlock RoDTEP/RoSCTL and US import

cons.claim: The finding is a structural argument, not a quantified one, so it persuades on direction not on a sized payoff
cons.example: arguing informality caps growth without a rupee figure for the foregone ceiling

failure_modes: mistaking off-paper for free margin rather than a low-ceiling risk
ignoring that rent scales up with the brand's own growth and visibility
acceptance_tests: off-paper is stated as a risk position carrying closure/lock-in/reassessment exposure and rent scaling with size, with informality framed as why these firms cannot grow
revisit_triggers: an enforcement shift changes the risk-reward of informality
the export-incentive regime changes the clean-docs payoff

nodes.definition: Characterize the labour reality: the workforce is ~90-95% migrant (FACT) from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, paid piece-rate against a Punjab statutory floor of ~Rs438/day unskilled (~Rs11,390/month, Mar-2025; skilled ~Rs487/day), compatible with the ILO comparative garment wage of ~US$145-172/month. The mechanism that makes the floor viable as a market wage is a low migrant survival basket (shared PG ~Rs8,000-8,500/month including food, work-tied housing saving ~Rs5,000-10,000/month) producing a low reservation wage, and housing-tied labour is less mobile and more retainable. The true migrant cash basket is UNKNOWN.

included: the ~Rs11-13k/month statutory floor and ILO comparative
excluded: the per-piece rate which is UNKNOWN (separate node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a minimum-wage notification or migrant-basket change updates the structure

pros.claim: Tying the floor to a migrant survival basket explains why ~Rs11-13k is a viable market wage and why housing-tied labour is retainable
pros.example: an entrant understanding that work-tied housing both lowers the reservation wage and reduces lean-season attrition

cons.claim: The statutory floor is the paper number, not the actual piece-rate take-home, which is UNKNOWN
cons.example: the floor stating ~Rs11,390/month while the real per-piece earnings stay unknown

failure_modes: using the statutory floor as if it were the actual labour cost
applying a middle-class living-cost basket to migrant wage reasoning
acceptance_tests: the ~90-95% migrant FACT, the ~Rs11-13k/month statutory floor, and the low-survival-basket reservation-wage mechanism are stated, with the true cash basket marked UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: a Punjab minimum-wage notification updates the floor
the migrant survival basket or housing-tie pattern changes

nodes.definition: Mark the per-piece sweater piece-rate in Ludhiana as the single most-wanted missing number and explicitly UNKNOWN: neither analyst found a reliable public figure and neither fabricated one. It is the input that blocks any honest bottom-up labour cost, and it must be obtained on the ground rather than guessed. This node exists to forbid fabrication and to flag that any labour cost built without it is incomplete; it is the highest-value open question in the whole operating-economics picture and the trigger that, once answered, would most change the model.

included: the per-piece rate as UNKNOWN and the #1 missing number
excluded: the statutory floor and migrant structure (parent node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reliable ground or published piece-rate figure is obtained

pros.claim: Naming the gap explicitly protects the model from a fabricated piece-rate masquerading as data
pros.example: a labour-cost line left explicitly incomplete rather than filled with an invented per-piece figure

cons.claim: Leaving the #1 input UNKNOWN means no honest bottom-up labour cost can be completed in this session
cons.example: a per-garment cost that cannot be closed until a ground piece-rate is obtained

failure_modes: fabricating a per-piece rate to complete a cost model
treating the statutory floor as a substitute for the missing piece-rate
acceptance_tests: the per-piece sweater rate is marked UNKNOWN and the #1 missing number, with fabrication explicitly forbidden and on-the-ground sourcing flagged
revisit_triggers: a reliable ground piece-rate figure is obtained
a credible published per-dozen rate appears

nodes.definition: Characterize the thekedar (labour contractor) layer as the mechanism that supplies and manages migrant piece-rate crews so the owner often does not employ workers directly, keeping wages low and headcount flexible. Read structurally, this is also the layer that absorbs headcount, identity, and cash, which is why it is the mechanism through which much of the off-paper economy is reported to operate, by keeping on-paper turnover and headcount under the regulatory thresholds. For a compliant entrant the cost is that running on-roll means paying the full loaded labour cost the off-roll competitor avoids; the layer itself is FACT, its use for threshold-evasion is the ESTIMATE inference.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: contract-labour regulation or an on-roll/off-roll gap sizing changes

pros.claim: Understanding the thekedar layer explains both why incumbent labour is cheap and why the compliant entrant cannot match it on labour cost
pros.example: an entrant accepting full on-roll loaded labour cost rather than routing crews off-roll through a contractor

cons.claim: The threshold-evasion reading is an ESTIMATE inference, not a documented act, so it informs mechanism not measurement
cons.example: treating contractor cash-absorption as a structural incentive rather than a proven practice

failure_modes: asserting a named contractor evades thresholds rather than describing the mechanism
assuming on-roll and off-roll labour cost the same
acceptance_tests: the thekedar layer is stated as FACT for labour supply, with its threshold-absorbing role as an ESTIMATE inference and the compliant full-loaded-cost consequence noted
revisit_triggers: contract-labour regulation changes the layer's use
a unit-level study sizes the on-roll vs off-roll gap

nodes.definition: Identify the two scarce skills that bound a small unit's quality and an AI-design pipeline's feasibility. Of the core roles (knitting panels, linking, checking, finishing), linking is where a small unit's quality reputation is won or lost: it joins panels at shoulder and side as the quality-critical seam, is eyesight-intensive and piece-rate, and skilled linkers are the recognized bottleneck and the hardest to re-hire after the lean season (ESTIMATE MED-HIGH). Separately, CAD/programmers for computerized flat-bed machines (Shima/Stoll-class) are scarce relative to operators of older hand/power-flat machines (ESTIMATE MED), a direct flag for an AI-design brand because the design pipeline assumes someone can translate a design into a machine program.

included: linking as the quality-critical eyesight-intensive bottleneck
CAD/flat-knit-programmer scarcity as the AI-pipeline flag
excluded: machine selection handled in the machines KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: linker/programmer availability or the machine skill mix changes

pros.claim: Naming linking and CAD-programming as the bottlenecks tells an AI-design brand exactly which scarce skills gate its quality and its pipeline
pros.example: an AI-design brand confirming a CAD/flat-knit programmer is available before assuming a design can be machine-programmed locally

cons.claim: The scarcity is a labeled estimate, so the staffability of the AI pipeline needs on-the-ground confirmation
cons.example: a programmer availability that looks adequate on paper but is tight in practice

failure_modes: assuming the AI-design-to-machine-program step is staffable without confirming programmer availability
treating linking as a commodity step rather than the quality-deciding bottleneck
acceptance_tests: linking is named as the quality-critical eyesight-intensive bottleneck and CAD/flat-knit-programmer scarcity is flagged for the AI pipeline, both labeled estimates
revisit_triggers: on-the-ground confirmation of programmer/linker availability
a shift toward whole-garment or automated machines changes the skill mix

nodes.definition: Establish that seasonality runs everything: the product is winter wear, order-lifting peaks around October, production ramps ~July-October, and there is a lean warm-season trough (FACT on the pattern; the exact month-by-month curve is UNKNOWN). This calendar is the root cause of the twin entrant shocks, because yarn is committed and goods are made months before cash returns and the migrant workforce contracts in the trough. Sizing working-capital headroom would need a unit-specific month-by-month volume curve, which is UNKNOWN here.

included: winter product, July-October ramp, October peak, lean trough FACT pattern
the calendar as root of the twin shocks

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a unit-specific seasonal volume curve or product-mix change updates the calendar

pros.claim: Fixing the calendar lets the brand anticipate the cash and labour pressure windows before they hit
pros.example: an entrant timing yarn commitment and credit headroom against the July-October ramp

cons.claim: The exact volume curve is UNKNOWN, so the calendar gives the shape but not the headroom magnitude
cons.example: knowing the ramp is July-October without a month-by-month curve to size working capital

failure_modes: treating demand as flat across the year
committing yarn without aligning to the ramp and trough
acceptance_tests: the winter product, July-October ramp, October peak, and lean trough are stated as the FACT pattern with the month-by-month curve marked UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: a unit-specific seasonal volume curve becomes known
the brand's product mix changes its seasonality

nodes.definition: Characterize the first twin shock: yarn is bought and goods are made months before cash returns, with receivables stretching across the winter season, so a seasonal-apparel cash cycle ties up working capital from the July-October ramp until post-peak collection (ESTIMATE: industry-lore, HIGH, as the standard seasonal-apparel cash cycle). This shock compounds the GST inverted-duty refund lag, because both trap working capital at the same time, and it is why a profitable-on-paper entrant can still be killed by the cash conversion cycle. The rupee magnitude depends on the UNKNOWN volume curve and yarn price.

included: the compounding with the GST inverted-duty lag
excluded: the landed-cost financing line handled in the logistics KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the cash gap becomes sizable or credit/refund terms change

pros.claim: Naming the working-capital shock and its overlap with the GST lag warns the brand that two cash traps coincide in-season
pros.example: an entrant sizing credit headroom to cover both the yarn-to-cash gap and the trapped GST refund at once

cons.claim: The shock's magnitude rests on the UNKNOWN volume curve and yarn price, so it is directional not sized
cons.example: knowing working capital is trapped in-season without a rupee headroom figure

failure_modes: under-provisioning credit for the in-season cash gap
missing that the GST lag and the cash cycle compound
acceptance_tests: the working-capital shock is stated as the yarn-before-cash seasonal cash cycle (ESTIMATE industry-lore HIGH) compounding the GST inverted-duty lag
revisit_triggers: the volume curve or yarn price lets the cash gap be sized
credit terms or the GST refund cycle change

nodes.definition: Characterize the second twin shock: in the lean warm-season trough migrants go home and may not return (FACT on the return pattern), and skilled linkers are the hardest to re-hire, so units over-pay or hoard core staff through the trough to keep the quality-critical seam staffed for the next ramp (ESTIMATE on the hoarding response). This shock interacts with the linker bottleneck, because the scarcest skill is also the least retainable, and with the housing-tie mechanism, because work-tied housing is the lever that reduces attrition. The cost of the hoarding response is real but its magnitude is UNKNOWN.

included: the linker re-hire difficulty and core-staff hoarding response ESTIMATE
excluded: the per-piece rate which is UNKNOWN

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the migrant return pattern or a retention-cost figure changes

pros.claim: Naming the retention shock tells the brand the scarcest skill is also the least retainable and must be planned for across the trough
pros.example: an entrant budgeting to retain core linkers through the lean season rather than assuming a fresh re-hire each ramp

cons.claim: The hoarding response is an ESTIMATE and its cost is UNKNOWN, so the shock is characterized not costed
cons.example: knowing core staff must be retained without a figure for the off-season retention cost

failure_modes: assuming linkers can be freshly re-hired each ramp
ignoring the housing-tie lever that reduces lean-season attrition
acceptance_tests: the migrant-return FACT and the linker-hoarding ESTIMATE response are stated, interacting with the linker bottleneck and the housing-tie retention lever
revisit_triggers: the migrant return pattern shifts
a retention-cost figure becomes known

nodes.definition: Assemble the recommended operating posture, the synthesis of the whole picture: because the entrant's edge can never be cost (the incumbents' model is the gap between paper cost and real cost, and a compliant newcomer pays the full paper cost while competing against people who do not), the realistic posture is compliant-core plus outsource-the-dirty-node (no dyehouse) plus explicitly budget BOTH the compliance-cost premium AND a friction/speed-money line item for discretionary approval gates, as planned named costs rather than surprises, and an arbitrage strategy. The edge is product (woollen/acrylic + AI design), brand, and US export-legitimacy, with the compliance premium a known line item. This is the consolidated artifact the owner operates from.

included: the two explicit budgeted line items
excluded: the brand/CAC and landed-cost models handled in other KBs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a statutory, enforcement, piece-rate, or seasonal change shifts the posture

pros.claim: One consolidated posture converts the scattered cost and political-economy findings into a single operating stance with two named budget lines
pros.example: an owner operating compliant-core, buying dyed yarn, and carrying explicit compliance-premium and friction line items from launch

cons.claim: The posture commits to a structurally higher landed cost whose competitor-gap magnitude is UNKNOWN, so it is a stance taken on direction not a sized optimum
cons.example: accepting a dearer compliant position without a rupee figure for the gap versus the price-setters

failure_modes: leaving the friction/speed-money line item off the budget so approval-gate cost is a surprise
drifting toward off-paper arbitrage and inheriting the low-ceiling risk
acceptance_tests: the posture states compliant-core, no-dyehouse, and BOTH a budgeted compliance-cost premium and a friction/speed-money line item, with the edge on product/brand/export-legitimacy not cost
revisit_triggers: a statutory rate, enforcement event, or piece-rate ground figure changes the cost picture
the season turns and the twin shocks re-engage

edges.why_related: the material-dominance anchor must be tagged FACT (54%) vs estimate (band) under the tagging discipline
the premium's direction-HIGH / magnitude-UNKNOWN labeling is governed by the tagging discipline
separating literature FACTs from cluster inference and barring accusation is the tagging discipline applied
the knit-garment stack is built on the material-dominance anchor with knitwear norms layered on
the spinning stack is built on the same material-dominance anchor with spinning norms layered on
the 15-25% labour line in the knit stack is what makes the EPF/ESI loading material to the premium
the EPF/ESI loading is the largest single legal component the premium assembles
the GST inverted-duty working-capital trap is a component of the assembled premium
the genuine effluent cost if dyeing is a component of the assembled premium
the headcount/turnover thresholds trigger the obligations the premium prices
the do-NOT-own-a-dyehouse judgment is the actionable conclusion of the effluent enforcement record
the six cluster mechanisms are ESTIMATE inferences drawn from the literature backbone FACTs
the threshold triggers are what the cash-dealing and under-invoicing mechanisms are reported to work around
the low-ceiling-risk finding is the owner conclusion drawn from the mechanisms
the labour line in the knit stack is filled out by the migrant piece-rate wage structure
the piece-rate UNKNOWN is the missing input within the migrant wage structure
the thekedar layer is the contracting mechanism that supplies the migrant crews
the thekedar's threshold-absorbing role is one of the off-paper mechanisms applied to labour
the linker and CAD-programmer scarcity is a specialization within the labour structure
the winter-seasonal calendar shapes when the dominant yarn cost is committed
the working-capital shock is the cash consequence of the seasonal calendar
the GST refund lag compounds the seasonal working-capital shock at the same time
the labour-retention shock is the workforce consequence of the seasonal trough
the scarcest linker skill is also the least retainable, sharpening the retention shock
the budgeted compliance premium is a core input to the compliant-core posture
outsource-the-dirty-node is a core element of the compliant-core posture
the low-ceiling-risk finding is why the posture rejects off-paper arbitrage
the EPF/ESI loading is one of the named budget lines the posture carries
the GST drag is folded into the budgeted premium of the posture
the seasonal cash trap is a planning input the posture must budget around
the retention shock is a labour-cost input the posture must budget around
the missing piece-rate bounds how completely the posture can size its labour line
a piece-rate ground figure or cost update routes the posture back to re-anchor the cost stack
running on-roll to carry the EPF/ESI loading competes head-to-head with routing labour off-roll through a thekedar to shed it
edges.resolution_rule: an export brand needing clean docs runs compliant on-roll and budgets the ~15%+ loading rather than routing labour off-roll, accepting the higher loaded cost as the price of export legitimacy

edges.why_related: outsourcing dyeing to avoid effluent risk surrenders the colour control that in-house dyeing within the finishing line would give
edges.resolution_rule: outsource dyeing or buy dyed yarn to push closure risk onto suppliers, accepting reduced colour control and adding an incoming-shade QC check rather than owning a dyehouse

edges.why_related: shedding the legal premium via off-paper arbitrage trades a near-term cost saving against the closure/lock-in/growth-cap risk
edges.resolution_rule: pay the legal premium as a budgeted line item rather than shed it off-paper, because the arbitrage is a low-ceiling risk position that caps growth and breaks export legitimacy

edges.why_related: the in-season cash squeeze causally tightens the funds available to over-pay or hoard core linkers through the trough

conflict_axes.name: on_roll_compliance_vs_off_roll_cost
conflict_axes.description: Running compliant on-roll labour carries the ~15%+ EPF/ESI loading and full statutory wages, while routing labour off-roll through a thekedar sheds it but builds the off-paper, low-ceiling, export-illegitimate position.
poles: route labour off-roll to shed loading
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: an export brand runs compliant on-roll and budgets the loading, because clean docs and legitimacy outweigh the off-roll saving

conflict_axes.name: paper_clean_premium_vs_off_paper_arbitrage
conflict_axes.description: Paying the legal compliance premium as a budgeted line item competes against shedding it via off-paper arbitrage that carries closure, lock-in, and growth-cap risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pay the premium; the off-paper route is a low-ceiling risk position, not free money, and breaks export legitimacy

conflict_axes.name: own_dyehouse_colour_control_vs_outsource_risk
conflict_axes.description: Owning a dyehouse gives colour control but inherits CETP non-compliance, NGT, and crore-penalty closure risk, while outsourcing pushes the risk onto suppliers at the cost of colour control.
poles: own the dyehouse for colour control
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: do not own a dyehouse; outsource or buy dyed yarn and add an incoming-shade QC check

conflict_axes.name: cost_edge_vs_product_brand_edge
conflict_axes.description: Chasing a cost edge against price-setters who shed the paper cost competes against competing on product, brand, and export-legitimacy where the compliant entrant can actually win.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the entrant's edge can never be cost; compete on woollen/acrylic + AI design, brand, and export-legitimacy

conflict_axes.name: threshold_growth_vs_lock_in_avoidance
conflict_axes.description: Crossing the EPF 20+ and Factories Act thresholds to scale on-roll competes against staying under them to avoid the once-covered-always-covered lock-in and full compliance load.
poles: stay under thresholds to avoid lock-in
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: for an export brand, cross deliberately and budget the lock-in, because staying fragmented under thresholds is the low-ceiling trap

conflict_axes.name: fresh_seasonal_commitment_vs_cash_preservation
conflict_axes.description: Committing yarn and building goods early to meet the October peak protects the season but deepens the working-capital trap, while staying lean preserves cash but risks missing the ramp.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: commit against confirmed orders and size credit headroom for the combined yarn-to-cash and GST-refund lag

conflict_axes.name: linker_retention_cost_vs_lean_season_release
conflict_axes.description: Over-paying or hoarding scarce linkers through the lean trough protects next-season quality but carries off-season cost, while releasing them saves cash but risks a re-hire failure on the quality-critical seam.
poles: retain core linkers through the trough
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: retain core linkers using the work-tied housing lever, because the scarcest skill is the least re-hireable

conflict_axes.name: statutory_floor_vs_unknown_piece_rate
conflict_axes.description: Costing labour off the known statutory floor is defensible but wrong for piece-rate work, while waiting for the UNKNOWN per-piece rate is honest but leaves the labour line open.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the floor only as a bound and mark the labour line incomplete until a ground piece-rate is obtained; never fabricate one

edge_cases.description: An analyst fabricates a per-piece sweater rate to complete a bottom-up labour cost
edge_cases.trigger: pressure to produce a finished labour-cost number with no ground piece-rate available
edge_cases.mitigation: leave the per-piece rate UNKNOWN and the labour line explicitly incomplete, flag it as the #1 on-the-ground number, and never invent a figure

edge_cases.description: An off-paper mechanism is stated as a named cluster firm's documented act rather than a structural mechanism
edge_cases.trigger: a discussion of speed money or under-invoicing names a specific firm or person
edge_cases.mitigation: rephrase as how clusters of this type are generally reported to operate, keep all amounts UNKNOWN, and implicate no named party

edge_cases.description: The entrant builds an in-house dyehouse to gain colour control and inherits a CETP-closure event
edge_cases.trigger: an NGT or CPCB action shuts non-compliant dyeing capacity the entrant now owns
edge_cases.mitigation: do not own a dyehouse; outsource or buy dyed yarn so closure risk sits with the supplier, and add an incoming-shade QC check

edge_cases.description: The entrant crosses the EPF 20+ threshold unaware it is once-covered-always-covered
edge_cases.trigger: on-roll headcount passes 20 and EPF coverage becomes permanent
edge_cases.mitigation: treat crossing 20+ as a deliberate permanent commitment and budget the EPF loading from the crossing forward

edge_cases.description: An acrylic/MMF brand is blindsided by the GST inverted-duty refund lag trapping working capital
edge_cases.trigger: input GST on MMF yarn accumulates as credit recoverable only through slow refunds
edge_cases.mitigation: budget the refund lag as trapped working capital that compounds the seasonal cash cycle and size credit headroom for both

edge_cases.description: Yarn is committed for the October peak and cash is trapped from the July-October ramp through collection
edge_cases.trigger: the seasonal cash cycle and the GST refund lag coincide in-season
edge_cases.mitigation: size working-capital headroom to cover the combined yarn-to-cash gap and GST refund lag, committing against confirmed orders

edge_cases.description: Skilled linkers do not return after the lean trough and the quality-critical seam is unstaffed at the ramp
edge_cases.trigger: migrants go home in the warm-season trough and core linkers cannot be re-hired
edge_cases.mitigation: retain core linkers through the trough using the work-tied housing lever rather than relying on a fresh re-hire each ramp

edge_cases.description: An AI-design brand assumes a design can be machine-programmed locally without a CAD/flat-knit programmer
edge_cases.trigger: the design-to-machine-program step is staffed only by operators of older flat machines
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm CAD/Shima-Stoll-class programmer availability on the ground before assuming the AI pipeline is staffable

edge_cases.description: The compliance premium is treated as zero because its competitor-gap magnitude is UNKNOWN
edge_cases.trigger: the gap to the price-setters cannot be sized in rupees, so it is dropped from the budget
edge_cases.mitigation: budget the premium on its HIGH-confidence direction as a named line item even while the competitor-gap magnitude stays UNKNOWN

edge_cases.description: The friction/speed-money line item is omitted so approval-gate cost arrives as a surprise
edge_cases.trigger: discretionary gates (pollution consent, GST-refund release, factory licence) impose delay-priced friction
edge_cases.mitigation: carry an explicit friction/speed-money line item as a planned cost for approval gates, not as an arbitrage strategy

edge_cases.description: The stale pre-2020 cluster output/export figures are quoted as current
edge_cases.trigger: the Rs5,000 cr output / Rs1,000-2,000 cr export figures are cited as today's numbers
edge_cases.mitigation: do not quote the stale figures as current; mark current post-2020 cluster output and export value UNKNOWN

edge_cases.description: The off-paper route is treated as a growth strategy rather than a low-ceiling survival one
edge_cases.trigger: an operator plans to scale on the back of off-paper cost savings
edge_cases.mitigation: treat off-paper as a low-ceiling risk position whose rent scales with size and that caps growth, and build the model paper-clean

workflow.description: Establish the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN rule, the no-named-accusation rule, and the no-fabricated-figure rule before any claim
workflow.gate: the labeling rule and the two prohibitions are stated and applied to every claim

workflow.action: Anchor material dominance on the one hard FACT
workflow.description: State yarn/material at ~50-60% anchored on the Vardhman FY20 54%-of-revenue FACT, band labeled estimate
workflow.gate: material is the ~50-60% dominant line on the 54% FACT with the band labeled an estimate

workflow.action: Lay out the knit-garment and spinning cost stacks
workflow.description: Give both labeled-estimate stacks (knit: yarn/labour/power; spinning: material/power/labour)
workflow.gate: both stacks are stated as labeled estimates with the dominant and decisive lines flagged

workflow.description: Bundle EPF/ESI + GST inverted-duty + effluent + statutory wages and the thresholds that trigger them
workflow.gate: the premium is assembled with direction HIGH and competitor-gap magnitude UNKNOWN

workflow.action: Quantify the EPF/ESI loading and the GST trap
workflow.description: State the ~15%+ EPF/ESI loading and the 12% GST inverted-duty working-capital trap acute for MMF
workflow.gate: the ~15%+ loading and the MMF inverted-duty trap are stated with the right tags

workflow.action: Establish effluent risk and the no-dyehouse judgment
workflow.description: Cite the CETP/NGT enforcement FACTs and conclude do-NOT-own-a-dyehouse, outsource or buy dyed yarn
workflow.gate: the enforcement FACTs and the no-dyehouse judgment with its tradeoff are stated

workflow.action: Frame the off-paper layer as mechanism not accusation
workflow.description: Give the literature backbone FACTs and the six mechanisms as ESTIMATE discussion with amounts UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the backbone FACTs and six mechanisms are stated with amounts UNKNOWN and no named-party accusation

workflow.description: Establish off-paper as a risk position not free money and informality as why these firms cannot grow
workflow.gate: off-paper is framed as a low-ceiling risk that caps growth and breaks export legitimacy

workflow.action: Characterize the migrant labour reality and the missing piece-rate
workflow.description: State the ~90-95% migrant workforce, the ~Rs11-13k floor, the thekedar layer, the bottlenecks, and the UNKNOWN piece-rate
workflow.gate: the migrant structure, thekedar, bottlenecks, and the UNKNOWN per-piece rate are stated

workflow.description: State the July-October winter ramp and the working-capital and labour-retention twin shocks
workflow.gate: the winter calendar and both twin shocks are stated with the month-by-month curve UNKNOWN

workflow.description: Compose compliant-core + no-dyehouse + budget-both-premiums with the edge on product/brand/legitimacy
workflow.gate: the posture states compliant-core, no-dyehouse, and both budgeted line items, edge not on cost

workflow.action: Set the review triggers for the cost and premium model
workflow.description: Define the triggers (ground piece-rate, statutory rate, enforcement event, season turn) that re-run the model
workflow.gate: an explicit trigger list routing back to the cost stack and posture exists

priority_rationale: The honesty tagging discipline and the single hard material-dominance FACT come first because every cost, regulation, and behaviour claim downstream depends on how it is labeled and on the one anchor that fixes where cost actually sits; the cost stacks and the compliance-premium components build the legal-cost picture; the off-paper nodes add the mechanism layer strictly as discussion with all amounts UNKNOWN and no named-party accusation; the labour and seasonality nodes add the piece-rate-UNKNOWN reality and the twin shocks; and the compliant-core posture comes last because it composes the premium, the no-dyehouse judgment, the low-ceiling-risk finding, and the seasonal/labour budget into one operating stance whose edge is product, brand, and export-legitimacy rather than a cost the entrant can never win.

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty tagging dominates any money, capacity, regulation, or behaviour claim
dominance_rules.rationale: an untagged estimate hardens into an apparent fact and an unframed mechanism becomes an accusation, both violating the binding discipline
dominance_rules.trigger: any such claim is about to be stated
dominance_rules.action: tag it FACT, ESTIMATE (method+basis+confidence), or UNKNOWN and frame off-paper as mechanism with amounts UNKNOWN

dominance_rules.rule: No fabricated named-firm figure ever substitutes for an UNKNOWN
dominance_rules.rationale: inventing a revenue, earnings, or piece-rate figure for a named firm breaks the financial-honesty charter and misleads planning
dominance_rules.trigger: a finished number is wanted but only an UNKNOWN exists
dominance_rules.action: leave it UNKNOWN and mark the line incomplete rather than fabricate

dominance_rules.rationale: naming a specific person or firm as bribing, evading, or being captured is barred and indefensible
dominance_rules.trigger: an off-paper mechanism is being described
dominance_rules.action: describe how clusters of this type are generally reported to operate, with all amounts UNKNOWN and no named party

dominance_rules.rule: Effluent closure risk dominates colour-control convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: owning a dyehouse inherits CETP-non-compliance, NGT, and crore-penalty closure risk that dwarfs the colour-control benefit
dominance_rules.trigger: an in-house dyehouse is considered for colour control
dominance_rules.action: outsource dyeing or buy dyed yarn and add an incoming-shade QC check instead

dominance_rules.rule: Export legitimacy dominates off-paper cost savings
dominance_rules.rationale: clean docs unlock RoDTEP/RoSCTL and US import and the bribery-performance literature finds export producers least harmed, so off-paper arbitrage is a low-ceiling trap
dominance_rules.trigger: off-paper arbitrage is considered as a cost edge
dominance_rules.action: run paper-clean and budget the legal premium as a named line item

dominance_rules.rule: The compliance premium is budgeted even when its magnitude is UNKNOWN
dominance_rules.rationale: the direction is HIGH-confidence, so dropping the premium because the competitor gap cannot be sized understates real cost
dominance_rules.action: carry the premium on its direction as a named budget line

dominance_rules.rule: The material-dominance anchor dominates generic cost assumptions
dominance_rules.rationale: yarn is half the stack, so the entrant's edge can never be input cost and margin must be sought downstream
dominance_rules.trigger: a cost-edge strategy is proposed at the factory gate
dominance_rules.action: anchor on material dominance and redirect the edge to product, brand, and distribution

dominance_rules.rule: Retaining the scarce linker dominates lean-season cash saving
dominance_rules.rationale: the quality-critical seam is the least re-hireable skill, so releasing it risks an unstaffed ramp that costs more than the off-season saving
dominance_rules.trigger: core linkers are considered for release in the trough
dominance_rules.action: retain them using the work-tied housing lever through the lean season

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the honesty tagging discipline before stating any substantive claim
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an estimate or mechanism later having to be relabeled or scrubbed of an accusation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Anchor the cost stack on the one hard FACT before building any premium on it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: premium math resting on an unanchored or wrongly-generalized cost share

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mark the per-piece rate UNKNOWN before any bottom-up labour cost is attempted
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fabricated piece-rate being baked into a labour model that must later be torn out

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide no-dyehouse before designing the finishing/colour workflow
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building an in-house dyeing line that inherits closure risk and must be unwound

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm CAD/flat-knit-programmer availability before committing the AI-design pipeline
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an AI-design-to-machine-program step that turns out unstaffable after commitment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Budget the compliance premium and a friction line item before pricing the product
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a price set without the legal premium and approval-gate friction that then cannot be recovered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size working-capital headroom for the combined seasonal and GST-refund lag before committing yarn
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a profitable-on-paper season killed by a cash trap that surfaces after yarn is committed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Plan core-linker retention before the lean trough, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unstaffed quality-critical seam at the ramp that no late re-hire can fill

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reliable on-the-ground per-piece sweater rate is obtained
iteration_protocol.action: re-open the labour line and re-run the knit-garment stack and the posture's labour budget

iteration_protocol.trigger: a statutory rate or threshold changes (EPF, ESI, GST, Factories Act, minimum wage)
iteration_protocol.action: re-quantify the affected premium component and re-assemble the compliance premium

iteration_protocol.trigger: an NGT/CPCB effluent enforcement event or a compliant small-scale dyeing option appears
iteration_protocol.action: re-assess the dyeing-risk node and the no-dyehouse judgment

iteration_protocol.trigger: the season turns toward the July-October ramp
iteration_protocol.action: re-engage the twin-shock planning and size combined working-capital headroom and linker retention

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new public-source FACT or peer-reviewed study supersedes an estimate or the off-paper backbone
iteration_protocol.action: re-tag the affected claim and update the material-dominance or off-paper nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: the brand's fibre/blend choice moves away from acrylic/MMF
iteration_protocol.action: re-assess whether the acute GST inverted-duty case still applies and re-cost the premium

iteration_protocol.trigger: on-the-ground confirmation of linker/CAD-programmer availability lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the bottleneck node and the AI-pipeline staffability assumption in the posture
